video_title: API Gateway: Why a Front Door for Microservices
core_insight: An API Gateway centralizes edge concerns for north-south traffic so clients stay stable while services change, but it must stay thin and stateless to avoid becoming a bottleneck and a hidden monolith.

scenes.voice: You have 20 to 40 microservices. Mobile apps, web, partners all need to call them. Why does this get messy fast?
scenes.visual: Multiple client icons pointing to many service boxes with tangled lines.

scenes.voice: Clients end up discovering the right service, handling retries, knowing versions, and dealing with different protocols. Each service re-implements auth, rate limiting, logging, TLS.
scenes.visual: Client box with checklist: discovery, retries, versions, protocols. Service boxes each with duplicated auth, rate limit, logging icons.
scenes.on_screen_text: Duplication in services, fragility in clients

scenes.voice: Centralizing that in services creates duplication and coupling. Scattering it in clients creates fragility. You need one stable entry point.
scenes.visual: Two bad patterns highlighted, then a single gateway icon appearing at edge.

scenes.voice: That is the API Gateway. Think front door and traffic cop, not business logic. All external requests enter here. It authenticates, shapes, and routes.
scenes.mermaid:
flowchart LR
    C[Client] --> G[API Gateway]
    G --> A[AuthN/Z]
    G --> R[Rate Limit]
    G --> S1[Service A]
    G --> S2[Service B]
    G --> S3[Service C]

scenes.voice: It does routing and optional composition, protocol translation, cross-cutting policy like auth, rate limiting, validation, caching, and observability. Services stay focused on domain logic.
scenes.visual: Gateway box with labels: Routing, Auth, Rate Limit, Transform, Logs/Metrics. Clean arrows to services.

scenes.voice: When does it help? Many external clients need a stable contract while backends change. You want one place for security, rate limiting, versioning. It decouples client contract from service topology.
scenes.visual: Client contract stable on left, services changing on right, gateway in middle bridging.

scenes.voice: Trade-offs: every request passes through it, so size it right or it adds latency and becomes a hot spot. It is a single point of failure, so run multi-zone active-active. And resist putting business logic here or you create a hidden monolith.
scenes.visual: Gateway with warning icons: latency, SPOF, business logic creep. Then checkmarks for stateless, horizontal scale, config-driven.

mental_model: Treat the API Gateway as a stateless edge traffic cop for north-south ingress only. It enforces cross-cutting concerns and hides service topology from clients. Keep it thin; business logic stays in services. Use service mesh for east-west.
final_takeaway: API Gateway centralizes edge concerns to decouple clients from services. Keep it stateless and thin, or it becomes a bottleneck and a hidden monolith.
